questions.question: Acceleration is defined as:
options: The change in velocity divided by the time taken — a = Δv/Δt
The change in position divided by the time taken

questions.question: The bus goes from rest to 15 m/s in 6 s. Its acceleration is:
options: 2,5 m/s² in the direction of motion

questions.question: While the bus cruises at a constant 15 m/s, its acceleration is:
options: Zero — the velocity is not changing
Negative, because the engine is idling

questions.question: Braking from 15 m/s to rest in 10 s gives an acceleration of:
options: −1,5 m/s² — the velocity loses 1,5 m/s every second

subtopics.title: The Position-Time Graph — Gradient Is Velocity

questions.question: The gradient of a position-time graph gives the:
A horizontal line on a position-time graph means the object is:
options: Stationary — position unchanged while time passes

questions.question: During the bus's pull-away, its position-time graph is:
options: An upward curve that steepens — each second covers more ground

questions.question: A straight line sloping downward on a position-time graph shows:
options: An object resting below the axis
Constant velocity in the negative direction — moving back towards the reference point

subtopics.title: The Velocity-Time Graph — Gradient and Area, Both Paying

questions.question: On a velocity-time graph, the gradient and the area under the graph give, respectively:
The braking segment falls from 15 m/s to 0 in 10 s. Its gradient is:
The displacement during the pull-away (0 to 15 m/s over 6 s) is the area of a triangle:
The total displacement for the whole journey (45 m + 450 m + 75 m) is:

subtopics.title: Reading All Three Graphs Together, and the Classic Traps

questions.question: For the bus's journey, the acceleration-time graph looks like:
options: Flat steps: 2,5 for 6 s, 0 for 30 s, −1,5 for 10 s
A single horizontal line at 2,5 m/s²

questions.question: The 'gradient down, area up' family links say that:
options: All three graphs share one shape
Gradients of position-time give velocity, and areas under velocity-time give displacement

questions.question: A rising straight line on a VELOCITY-time graph means the object is:
options: Moving away from the start at constant speed
Speeding up — not 'moving away', which is the classic misreading

questions.question: On a velocity-time graph, an object at REST is shown by:
options: A horizontal line at any height
A line lying on the time axis itself

questions.question: In the needle picture, acceleration measures:
options: How fast the speedometer needle itself is moving
How fast the bus is moving
How far the bus has travelled
How hard the engine is working

questions.question: 'Two and a half metres per second, per second' means:
options: The bus covers 2,5 m every second
Every second, the velocity grows by another 2,5 m/s
The bus's top speed is 2,5 m/s
The needle spins 2,5 times per second

questions.question: A resting needle at 15 m/s means:
options: Zero acceleration while moving fast — the speed is simply not changing

questions.question: Passengers are tipped forward during which phase?
options: No phase — passengers cannot feel acceleration
The braking — the needle sinking as velocity is lost

questions.question: The bus trip's velocity-time silhouette is:
On the silhouette, steepness represents:
options: Acceleration — the driver's feet on accelerator or brake

questions.question: The falling ramp at the end of the graph means the bus:
options: Slowed while still moving forward — height is speed, not position

questions.question: The bus would only be moving backwards if the velocity-time graph:

subtopics.title: The Area That Pays Out in Metres

questions.question: The area under a velocity-time graph equals the:
The cruising plateau, 15 m/s for 30 s, contributes an area of:
options: 450 m — the rectangle height times width

questions.question: The pull-away triangle is HALF of the full-speed rectangle because:
options: Triangles are always half of everything
The axes are drawn to scale
Speeding up from rest, the bus averaged only half its top speed
Half is removed for the driver's reaction time

questions.question: The braking triangle, ½ × 10 s × 15 m/s, gives a stopping distance of:
